name: Vulnerability Scanning & Assessment
tagline: Automated detection of known CVEs and misconfigurations at scale, plus manual triage.

tools.name: Nmap
tools.desc: The de-facto open-source network scanner: host discovery, port scanning, OS and service fingerprinting, and NSE scripts for scripted vulnerability checks.
tools.when: Baseline port and service enumeration across your own servers before deeper targeted testing.

tools.name: nmap-vulners NSE
tools.desc: An Nmap script pair (vulners.nse / vulscan.nse) that queries the Vulners API with each scanned software version and prints matching CVEs next to the banner.
tools.when: Turning a routine nmap scan of services you operate into an instant CVE snapshot with no extra tooling.

tools.name: Masscan
tools.desc: Robert Graham's asynchronous parallel scanner that can sweep all 65k ports of an address range in minutes using raw SYN packets.
tools.when: Large authorized perimeter sweeps where nmap's serialized timing would take too long, followed by nmap for detail.

tools.name: RustScan
tools.desc: Rust-based port scanner that finds open ports in seconds, then pipes them straight into nmap for full service discovery.
tools.when: Fast first-pass open-port identification when running a full nmap -p- on your hosts is too slow.

tools.name: arp-scan
tools.desc: ARP-based discovery that maps every live host and MAC vendor on the local segment you operate, including those ignoring ping.
tools.when: Inventorying the devices on a LAN you administer before running port scans against them.

tools.name: netdiscover
tools.desc: Active (ARP request) and passive (sniff-and-log) network discovery with a lightweight interactive frame view of the subnet.
tools.when: Live host discovery on switched networks you manage without agents.

tools.name: ZMap
tools.desc: High-performance network scanner built for internet-wide research on services you own; the engine behind the ZMap project ('there are no secrets on the internet').
tools.when: Measuring the exposed surface of your own public address space in collaboration with your network ops team.

tools.name: AutoRecon
tools.desc: Tib3rius's recon orchestrator that runs nmap, service enumeration, web scans, and vulnerability checks in parallel and writes per-host reports you can review.
tools.when: Structured, repeatable external assessment of an IP range you are authorized to test.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/Tib3rius/AutoRecon && cd AutoRecon && pip3 install -r requirements.txt

tools.name: Nettacker
tools.desc: OWASP scanner framework that scans layers of your network (ports, services, subdomains), correlates results, then runs follow-up module checks.
tools.when: One-pass automated network discovery plus vulnerability probing across the infrastructure you own.

tools.name: WhatWeb
tools.desc: Ruby web fingerprinting tool identifying the platform, CMS, JavaScript libraries, and headers behind over 1,800 technology signatures.
tools.when: Telling what stack a web property you own runs before picking follow-up scanners.

tools.name: Nikto
tools.desc: Perl web server scanner running 7,000+ checks for known files, outdated software, and misconfigurations on your own sites.
tools.when: Fast baseline sweep of a web server's exposed surface before deeper application testing.

tools.name: wafw00f
tools.desc: Identifies whether and which WAF (Cloudflare, ModSecurity, AWS WAF, etc.) fronts a web property, and fingerprints its version where detectable.
tools.when: Checking what edge protection sits in front of your applications before sending scan traffic through it.

tools.name: OWASP ZAP
tools.desc: Full-featured open-source web app scanner combining an intercepting proxy, spidering, and automated active and passive scanning behind a REST API.
tools.when: DAST runs against the apps you build, or as the intercepting proxy for manual test sessions.

tools.name: Wapiti
tools.desc: Command-line web fuzzer performing black-box scans for SQLi, XSS, file inclusion, SSRF, and more, without needing a browser.
tools.when: Scriptable, headless DAST batches over many of your endpoints in CI.

tools.name: Nuclei
tools.desc: ProjectDiscovery's template engine running thousands of YAML checks against web, network, and infrastructure targets to confirm known CVEs and misconfigurations.
tools.when: First-pass automated sweep across a whole asset list; fast and CI-friendly enough to run on every build.

tools.name: sqlmap
tools.desc: Long-standing automated SQL injection detector with database fingerprinting; validates whether a suspected injection point on your own app is genuinely exploitable.
tools.when: Confirming and triaging reported SQLi findings on applications you own and operate.

tools.name: dalfox
tools.desc: Fast Go-based XSS scanner that fuzzes parameters, builds payloads, and verifies reflected and stored vectors against the pages you maintain.
tools.when: Payload-based validation of XSS candidates found by DAST tools on your own endpoints.

tools.name: WPScan
tools.desc: WordPress scanner that fingerprints core, theme, and plugin versions against the WPScan vulnerability database and does user and weak-password checks.
tools.when: Regularly auditing the WordPress sites you maintain for outdated plugins and known CVEs.

tools.name: CMSmap
tools.desc: Python tool that scans WordPress, Joomla, and Drupal sites you own for known vulnerabilities and exposed file paths.
tools.when: A single-command health check across mixed small-CMS estates without installing separate scanners.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/Dionach/CMSmap && pip3 install -r CMSmap/requirements.txt

tools.name: droopescan
tools.desc: Lightweight Perl scanner focused on Drupal, with partial WordPress and Bolt coverage; strong on plugin and module fingerprinting.
tools.when: Targeted assessments of the Drupal sites in your fleet.

tools.name: Nessus
tools.desc: Tenable's market-standard commercial scanner with credentialed and remote checks across OSes, services, and web; the free Essentials tier covers a small lab.
tools.when: Deep credentialed findings and compliance-style reports on the servers you operate.
tools.install: Download Nessus *.deb from tenable.com and run: sudo dpkg -i Nessus-*.deb

tools.name: OpenVAS (GVM)
tools.desc: Greenbone's open-source stack forked from the old Nessus; schedules scans of thousands of network vulnerability tests (NVTs) with a web dashboard.
tools.when: Self-hosted, ongoing internal-network scanning without commercial licensing.
tools.install: sudo apt install gvm && sudo gvm-setup

tools.name: Vuls
tools.desc: Agentless Go scanner that runs from one control host over SSH to inventory OS packages, middleware, and containers, then maps each server to applicable CVEs.
tools.when: Fleet-level Linux vulnerability tracking when installing agents on every box is not an option.

tools.name: Lynis
tools.desc: Security auditing tool that runs 300+ tests on Unix systems to score hardening posture and flag misconfigurations, missing patches, and weak settings.
tools.when: Whole-box hardening reviews of the Linux servers you run, on demand or scheduled.

tools.name: OpenSCAP
tools.desc: NIST-certified scanner applying security-policy content (CIS, STIG) and OVAL CVE definitions to your Linux hosts for compliance and vulnerability posture.
tools.when: Auditing your servers against published baselines and tracking CVE coverage across them.

tools.name: Pacu
tools.desc: Rhino Security Labs' AWS exploitation framework with modules for privilege escalation, lateral movement, and misconfiguration chaining against accounts you own.
tools.when: Testing the blast radius of an IAM misconfiguration in your own AWS account during a red-team exercise.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/RhinoSecurityLabs/pacu && cd pacu && bash install.sh

tools.name: Prowler
tools.desc: Cloud security tooling applying 200+ AWS (and Azure/GCP) checks aligned to CIS, NIST, and ISO to surface misconfigurations in accounts you operate.
tools.when: Automated compliance sweeps of your cloud accounts before audits.

tools.name: ScoutSuite
tools.desc: Security audit tool from NCC Group that uses cloud APIs to enumerate resources and generate an HTML report of weaknesses across AWS, Azure, and GCP.
tools.when: Read-only posture reviews of your cloud subscriptions summarized into one report.

tools.name: Trivy
tools.desc: Aqua's scanner that fingerprints vulnerable packages and CVEs in the container images, filesystems, IaC templates, and SBOMs you run.
tools.when: Adding vuln gates to your image builds and scanning local containers for known CVEs before deployment.

tools.name: Grype
tools.desc: Anchore's fast scanner pairing with Syft to map dependency CVEs across the containers and filesystems you build and ship.
tools.when: Container and directory scans where you also want an SBOM generated in the same workflow.

tools.name: Syft
tools.desc: Generates an inventory/SBOM of the packages, libraries, and metadata inside container images and directory trees, feeding downstream scanners.
tools.when: Getting a machine-readable software bill of materials for the images you build, then diffing against CVE feeds.

tools.name: Clair
tools.desc: Quay's open-source static analyzer that watches container registries and reports vulnerabilities in each image's layers via a JSON API.
tools.when: Continuous scanning of the container registry you operate so images are screened before and after push.

tools.name: Snyk
tools.desc: Developer-focused SCA platform with a free CLI that maps your manifest and lockfiles to known vulnerabilities and suggests upgrades.
tools.when: Fast triage of dependency findings in your repos with remediation hints.

tools.name: osv-scanner
tools.desc: Google's scanner that matches your project lockfiles and SBOMs against the open-source-focused OSV.dev vulnerability database.
tools.when: Quick CI check of dependency lockfiles in your own repos against a community-maintained vuln feed.

tools.name: pip-audit
tools.desc: PyPA's scanner that audits installed Python packages and lockfiles against the OSV and PyPI advisory feeds, with a fix action.
tools.when: Adding a pip dependency check to your Python projects' CI pipelines.

tools.name: npm audit
tools.desc: Built-in npm command that checks package-lock.json against the npm advisory database and proposes non-breaking or breaking upgrades.
tools.when: Dependency health checks in JS projects you maintain, straight from your package manager.

tools.name: cve-bin-tool
tools.desc: Scans binary files and their strings to identify which known-vulnerable library and product components your software bundles.
tools.when: Checking compiled products you distribute for embedded third-party components with published CVEs.

tools.name: NVD
tools.desc: Official NIST vulnerability feed and web UI; the reference source for CVE metadata, CPE mappings, and CVSS metrics.
tools.when: Confirming identifiers, severity scores, and affected product lists for a CVE under review.
tools.install: preinstalled (web + free REST API, no install)

tools.name: CVE.org
tools.desc: The CVE Program's own record search and API maintained by MITRE, giving canonical descriptions, references, and reservation workflows.
tools.when: Reading the authoritative record and reference list for a given CVE-ID.

tools.name: Vulners
tools.desc: Aggregated vulnerability and exploit database offering a free API plus the vulners.nse Nmap script that matches your scanned services against millions of CVEs.
tools.when: Enriching plain nmap service banners of your hosts with live CVE matches at no cost.
tools.install: pip3 install vulners  (or query the REST API)

tools.name: cve-search
tools.desc: Local MongoDB-backed engine that ingests NVD, CISA, and Exploit-DB feeds for fast bulk lookups across your whole inventory.
tools.when: Correlating a large asset list against CVE data offline when you cannot rely on external APIs.

tools.name: OSV.dev
tools.desc: Google's open-source-oriented vulnerability database with a query API keyed on affected package/ecosystem plus a public, continuous-export data feed.
tools.when: Programmatic lookup of vulnerabilities for the exact package versions in your SBOM or lockfile.

tools.name: Exploit-DB / searchsploit
tools.desc: Offline grep over the ~40,000-entry Exploit-DB archive bundled with Kali, showing exploit scripts, Metasploit modules, and build instructions for your own lab.
tools.when: Looking up local proof-of-concept code to reproduce and verify a CVE on systems you control.

tools.name: Metasploit Framework
tools.desc: Rapid7's exploit framework whose auxiliary and exploit modules double as scanners, with searchsploit-backed proof-of-concept modules for verified CVEs.
tools.when: Reproducing a known CVE against your lab systems and deploying the matching exploit module in a controlled environment.
